sections.label: Three enablers for AI advantage

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha

sections.label: Singapore cyberattacks and ransomware
sections.summary: The 2018 SingHealth cyberattack compromised 1.5 million patients' data, and 255 firms linked to critical infrastructures were allegedly targeted, with ransomware disrupting healthcare clusters and vendors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
sentences.text: The 2018 SingHealth cyberattack compromised the data of 1.5 million patients.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
sentences.text: More recently, it was reported that 255 firms linked to Singapore's critical infrastructures were allegedly targeted and ransomware incidents have disrupted healthcare clusters and third party vendors.

sections.label: Digital conflict and national survival
sections.summary: Escalating digital conflict makes resilience necessary, as intrusions with dormant malicious code could disrupt telecommunications, payment and transport systems and cripple SAF mobilisation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
sentences.text: In a world of escalating digital conflict, resilience is not optional.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
sentences.text: Trust in our digital economy depends on our ability to defend it.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
sentences.text: We must ensure that as Singapore digitises at scale, our cybersecurity posture strengthens at equal speed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Such intrusions are a stark reminder that the digital battle space has expanded into a theatre of strategic sabotage, APT actors, prepositioned malicious code to sit dormant for years, designed to be activated during a crisis to trigger power failures or disrupt transport and payment systems.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: For Singapore, this poses a direct threat to our national survival as a coordinated disruption to civilian telecommunications, payment systems and transport networks would directly cripple the Singapore Armed Force's ability to mobilise and deploy troops at speed.

sections.label: Joint assessment of Quantum Key Distribution

sentences.text: In January 2024, the cybersecurity agencies of France, Germany, the Netherlands and Sweden jointly assessed Quantum Key Distribution (QKD).

sentences.text: Australia's deadline to cease classical public key cryptography is in 2030; Japan, 2035; 18 EU states signed a PQC commitment last November.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: TikTok is designated under our own code of practice, and the commission found that its screen time tools and parental controls do not effectively address these risks.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: One, does the code of practice require designated services to submit a design risk assessment, covering recommendation systems, auto play and scroll architecture?

sentences.text: In a survey of 250 local employers, 80% acknowledged that AI has already reduced their entry-level hiring.

sentences.text: Budget 2026 sets a clear direction: a National AI Council chaired by the Prime Minister and national AI Missions to drive real outcomes across advanced manufacturing, connectivity, finance and healthcare.

sentences.text: Budget measures, such as expanding the Enterprise Innovation Scheme to support qualifying AI expenditures can spur uptake.

sentences.text: How will the Champions of AI programme sit alongside schemes like the Enterprise Innovation Scheme and the Productivity Solutions Grant, given that they are administered by different statutory boards under different Ministries?

sections.label: IT firms and AI know-how
sections.summary: The passage asks whether MDDI can work with top AI firms and hyperscalers to transfer know-hows to local firms, and whether GovTech can embrace these approaches and require IT service companies in Government work to do the same.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: Singapore's IT services firms are the delivery layer between our national AI strategy and real-world outcomes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: Can MDDI work with the top AI firms and hyperscalers already based here to transfer such know-hows to our local firms?

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: Can the Government Technology Agency of Singapore (GovTech) also move quickly to embrace these approaches, while adhering to cybersecurity and regulatory requirements, and progressively require IT service companies involved in Government work to do the same?

sections.label: Public Service Media headwinds
sections.summary: Public Service Media face significant headwinds: declining circulation in a fragmented media space, a rapidly evolving advertising model and growing disinformation from overseas.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: Yet, our Public Service Media face significant headwinds, declining circulation in a fragmented media space, a rapidly evolving advertising model and growing disinformation from overseas.

sections.summary: The question asks whether the same can be done so that local content quality is not buried by algorithms favouring overseas programming.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: Can we do the same, so that the quality of local content is not buried by algorithms favouring overseas programming?

sections.label: Fake reports about leaders
sections.summary: Many people read fake online reports claiming Senior Minister Lee publicly disagreed with Prime Minister Wong.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
sentences.text: Most recently, many of us would have read about the fake reports online claiming that Senior Minister Lee publicly disagreed with Prime Minister Wong.

sections.label: AI threat and Public Service Media
sections.summary: AI worsens the threat by generating convincing content at scale and probing critical information infrastructure, and the question asks how Government will strengthen Public Service Media against fake news.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
sentences.text: AI worsens the threat because it can generate convincing content at scale, iterate rapidly and be used to probe and undermine our critical information infrastructure.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
sentences.text: First, how will the Government support and strengthen our Public Service Media so it can more effectively in countering fake news and misinformation in an increasingly noisy information environment?

sections.label: Singapore global AI governance role
sections.summary: Singapore led with the Model AI Governance Framework and work on Generative and Agentic AI, and the question asks what more Government will do on global AI governance.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
sentences.text: Singapore has led with the Model AI Governance Framework of January 2019, a world first, and followed up with work on Generative and Agentic AI.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
sentences.text: Internationally, we could forge norms that prevent regulatory arbitrage and ensure cross‑border accountability.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
sentences.text: Hence, building on existing frameworks, what more will the Government do to strengthen Singapore's role in global AI governance, standards, certification, international coordination and capacity building, to preserve human agency while responsibly constraining AI agency?

sections.label: Four AI safety proposals
sections.summary: Four proposals: a national AI safety curriculum, OSC incorporating AI-specific risks, a public-private AI anti-scam taskforce, and community-based digital safety ambassadors.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: One, introduce a national AI safety curriculum across digital literacy programmes for different age groups and life stages.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: Two, the Online Safety Commission (OSC) can incorporate AI-specific risks into its categories of online harms by recognising AI-generated impersonations such as deepfakes and mass production of inauthentic materials to enable victims to seek timely remedies.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: Three, establish a public-private AI anti-scam taskforce to stay ahead of evolving threats and coordinate responses.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: Four, leveraging the base of Digital Ambassadors, develop a network of community-based digital safety ambassadors focused on AI risks in senior activity centres, schools and social service settings.

sections.label: Targeted rules for frontier AI
sections.summary: Frontier AI models pose a different category of risk, so Singapore should move toward targeted requirements for high-risk or high-impact AI systems rather than broad, one-size-fits-all.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: And frontier AI models, the most powerful and unpredictable, pose a different category of risk altogether.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: That is why I believe Singapore should move toward targeted requirements for high‑risk or high‑impact AI systems rather than broad, one‑size‑fits‑all.

sections.label: SME AI adoption and workforce support
sections.summary: The passage asks how SMEs can tap champions for governance support and sets out role-specific skill maps, training, and Budget and Cyber Resilience Centre support for AI adoption.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: Can MDDI share how SMEs can tap these champions for governance support, workflow redesign and to fully leverage national compute and enterprise schemes?

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: The workforce transformation roadmaps must go beyond broad skills.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: Workers need role‑specific skill maps to show how tasks will change with AI, clear pathways to move from today's roles to tomorrow's AI‑enabled, and hands‑on training tied to tools that SMEs are actually adopting.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: When workers see how AI makes work easier and raises productivity, adoption becomes natural.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: I welcome the Budget's investment in local AI developers and testbeds and the role of Government procurement in helping them scale.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: And as AI becomes more embedded in operations, the new Cyber Resilience Centre and enhanced SME support will give businesses the confidence to adopt AI safely.

sections.label: National AI Impact Programme
sections.summary: MDDI is creating the National AI Impact Programme, which aims to support 10,000 local enterprises to integrate AI over three years.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Digital Development and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: At stake are our entrepreneurs' hopes and dreams, workers' livelihoods and their communities' progress.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Digital Development and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: This is why MDDI is creating the National AI Impact Programme – to turn AI's possibilities into reality for the many, not the few.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Digital Development and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Today, 15% of SMEs and about seven in 10 workers use AI in some way.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Digital Development and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Over the next three years, the National AI Impact Programme aims to support 10,000 local enterprises to integrate AI into their business processes.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Digital Development and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: There are now many AI tools that improve business operations in simple, effective ways.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Digital Development and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: They make up 30% of the digital solutions on IMDA's SMEs Go Digital platform today.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Digital Development and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Often, the technology is ready, but people are not.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Digital Development and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: This is why we are enhancing the Digital Leaders Programme and launching a new Digital Leaders Accelerator Bootcamp to build skills and confidence in change management and not just tech capabilities.

sections.label: Supporting AI bilingual workers

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Digital Development and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: For a start, the Government will support 100,000 workers to become AI bilingual.

sections.summary: IMDA will work with agencies and professional bodies to expand its TeSA programme to develop AI bilingual workers in key domains.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Digital Development and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: IMDA will work with relevant agencies and professional bodies to expand its TeSA programme, to develop AI bilingual workers in key domains.

sections.label: Model Governance Framework for Agentic AI
sections.summary: A new Model Governance Framework for Agentic AI will help organisations manage systems that act with greater independence while ensuring human oversight.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Digital Development and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Our new Model Governance Framework for Agentic AI will help organisations manage systems that can act with greater independence, while ensuring human oversight.

sections.label: Singapore chairmanship of UN working group

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Digital Development and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: On the diplomatic front, Singapore recently concluded our chairmanship of the Second UN Open-Ended Working Group on security of and in the use of info-comm technologies.

sentences.text: First, we will review our cybersecurity standards and requirements for CII owners.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Digital Development and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Second, we will provide CII owners with advanced tools, so that they are equipped to deal with advanced threats and.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Digital Development and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Third, we will work with partners to build up capabilities in our cybersecurity workforce.

sections.label: IMDA enhancing telecommunications cybersecurity regulations
sections.summary: IMDA will be enhancing its cybersecurity regulations for telecommunications operators given the recent waves of attacks.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
sentences.text: For example, IMDA will be enhancing its cybersecurity regulations for the telecommunications operators, given the recent waves of attacks.

sections.label: Sharing government expertise with CII owners
sections.summary: The Government will share classified threat intelligence and proprietary threat detection systems with CII owners to help them counter APTs.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
sentences.text: Typically, national security is the exclusive domain of governments, such as developing cutting-edge technological systems and training skilled operators to deal with various threat scenarios.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
sentences.text: We have decided to avail some of the Government’s expertise to the private sector, to level the playing field between the defenders and the attackers.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
sentences.text: We will help our CII owners “level up” and hold their own in a fight against APTs.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
sentences.text: We will selectively share classified threat intelligence with our CII owners so that they are better able to spot and respond swiftly to threats that are attacking their systems.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
sentences.text: We will equip CII owners with proprietary threat detection systems to strengthen their abilities to detect malicious activities in their networks, especially those of state-sponsored APTs.

sections.label: Minimum cybersecurity requirements for routers

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
sentences.text: CSA and IMDA therefore intend to raise the minimum cybersecurity requirements for all routers sold in Singapore to the equivalent of CLS Level 2.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
sentences.text: To better protect citizens, CSA will explore requiring IP cameras to meet CLS Level 2, similar to home routers.

sentences.text: GovTech will require Government vendors that manage critical systems and sensitive government data to meet Cyber Trust Mark requirements.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
sentences.text: Consultations with relevant stakeholders are ongoing and these measures will be implemented progressively over the next two years.

sections.label: Training and quantum-safe networks
sections.summary: The Government is working with industry experts on training and deploying two quantum-safe networks through the NQSN+ initiative.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
sentences.text: We are working with industry experts to better support organisations in their efforts, including through training.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
sentences.text: We are also deploying two quantum-safe networks nationwide through the National Quantum Safe Network Plus (NQSN+) initiative.

sentences.text: Scribe is now used in over 100 social service agencies and all public healthcare institutions.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau)
sentences.text: On average, 36 minutes are saved on documentation per conversation.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau)
sentences.text: By doing this, their enhanced Vaping Information System was live in just three weeks.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau)
sentences.text: A system built from scratch, would have taken months.

sections.label: GovTech agentic AI coding tools pilot

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau)
sentences.text: GovTech is also piloting agentic AI coding tools internally and plans to expand these capabilities across Government.

sections.label: Oobee website scans

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau)
sentences.text: Oobee has scanned over 1,600 websites since 2023.

sections.label: SIM card limit and scam analytics
sections.summary: IMDA implemented a limit of 10 postpaid SIM cards per person across all telcos, and the Government will apply analytics to SIM card registration data to detect and disrupt scam activities.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau)
sentences.text: To address this, IMDA, in consultation with the Singapore Police Force, recently implemented a limit of 10 postpaid SIM cards per person across all telcos.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau)
sentences.text: The Government will also apply analytics to SIM card registration data, within strict legal safeguards, to proactively detect and disrupt potential scam activities.

sections.label: Institute of Digital Government establishment
sections.summary: MDDI will establish the Institute of Digital Government together with the Civil Service College.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau)
sentences.text: MDDI will establish the Institute of Digital Government together with the Civil Service College.

sections.label: SupportGoWhere consolidates government schemes
sections.summary: The SupportGoWhere portal consolidates Government schemes across 31 agencies.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau)
sentences.text: Take the SupportGoWhere portal, which consolidates Government schemes across 31 agencies.

sections.label: Streamlining healthcare professional registration
sections.summary: Processes are simplified and the Professional Registration System rebuilt, cutting foreign nurse registration from up to six months to 30 days.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau)
sentences.text: Lengthy manual registration processes to bring in nurses can become a bottleneck that delays care.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau)
sentences.text: And that is why we are simplifying our processes and rebuilding the Professional Registration System to streamline and automate routine checks for our healthcare professionals.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau)
sentences.text: We have reduced processing time for foreign nurse registrations from up to six months to 30 days.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau)
sentences.text: For patients and families waiting for care, this can mean earlier treatment, earlier support and less anxiety.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau)
sentences.text: All of us working in Government must ask ourselves: if we are responsible for a policy, is it being delivered in the simplest way possible?

sections.label: Singaporeans compare digital experiences
sections.summary: Singaporeans increasingly compare Government to the best digital experiences in their daily lives, not just to other governments.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau)
sentences.text: Increasingly, Singaporeans compare us to the best digital experiences in their daily lives, not just to governments elsewhere.

sections.label: Online Safety Commission established
sections.summary: The Online Safety (Relief and Accountability) Act establishes the Online Safety Commission, set up by the first half of this year, supporting victims of five online harms.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: As part of the Online Safety (Relief and Accountability) Act, we will establish a new agency, the Online Safety Commission (OSC).

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: The OSC will be set up by the first half of this year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: It will begin by supporting victims of five highly prevalent and severe online harms: online harassment; intimate image abuse; image-based child abuse; doxxing; and online stalking.

sections.label: App store age assurance measures
sections.summary: From the end of this month, designated app stores must implement age assurance measures to prevent under-18 users accessing age-inappropriate apps.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: From the end of this month, designated app stores will have to implement age assurance measures to prevent users who are under 18 from accessing and downloading age-inappropriate apps.

sections.label: Extending age assurance to social media
sections.summary: As MDDI studies the impact of social media bans, it plans to extend age assurance requirements to designated social media services.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: As MDDI continues to study the impact of social media bans, we plan to extend age assurance requirements to designated social media services.

sections.label: Smart Nation Educator Fellowship launch
sections.summary: MDDI and MOE launched the Smart Nation Educator Fellowship last year, with 58 fellows in the inaugural run.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: Last year, MDDI and MOE launched the Smart Nation Educator Fellowship, and 58 fellows attended the inaugural run.

sections.label: Code for Fun AI update
sections.summary: IMDA and MOE are updating the Code for Fun programme to integrate AI skills for all students, available to all schools in 2027.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: IMDA is working with MOE to update the Code for Fun programme in our primary and secondary schools to integrate AI skills as core baseline capabilities for all students.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: We will make this available to all schools in 2027.

sections.label: DigitalAccess@Home for lower-income families
sections.summary: IMDA's DigitalAccess@Home scheme will continue supporting lower-income families with subsidised broadband and computing devices.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: For lower-income families, IMDA's DigitalAccess@Home scheme will continue to support them with subsidised broadband and computing devices.

sections.label: NLB SURE information literacy rollout
sections.summary: NLB will roll out new resource packages and outreach programmes under SURE to build information literacy skills.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: NLB will roll out new resource packages and outreach programmes under SURE to build information literacy skills.

sections.label: Langkah Digital for Malay/Muslim community
sections.summary: M³ launched Langkah Digital, led by Yayasan MENDAKI, designed around three elements: Kenal, Guna, Yakin.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: To work towards making our vision of an AI-Confident Malay/Muslim community a reality, M³ has launched Langkah Digital, led by Yayasan MENDAKI.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: As I announced last month, Langkah Digital is designed around three key elements – Kenal, Guna, Yakin.

sections.label: AI workshops community participation
sections.summary: Twelve AI-related workshops and events have been rolled out in the community, reaching over 400 participants.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: Although I just launched the programme last month, I am heartened that we have rolled out 12 AI-related workshops and events in the community so far, reaching over 400 participants.

sections.label: SG60 book and exhibition
sections.summary: NLB and MDDI launched a book and exhibition on The Albatross File, visited by over 130,000 since December.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: To mark Singapore's 60 years of Independence, NLB and MDDI launched a book and exhibition on The Albatross File, which documents the events, personalities and debates surrounding Singapore's journey to Independence.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: Since December, over 130,000 have visited; 96% said they left with a deeper understanding of the path Singapore took.

sections.label: Freedom of Information Act proposal
sections.summary: Documents were published in full without redaction, and Mr Fadli raised a Freedom of Information Act proposal.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: The documents published were reproduced in full, without redaction.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: Mr Fadli also raised the proposal for a Freedom of Information Act to automatically declassify records and release them publicly after 25 years.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: In fact, implementing an Freedom of Information Act could lead unintentionally to more opacity.

sections.label: Transparency for good governance
sections.summary: A Freedom of Information Act can hinder governance, so transparency should prioritise good governance and an informed citizenry.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: It's a thoroughly bad way of analysing complex issues." In other words, a Freedom of Information Act can hinder rather than facilitate governance because issues deemed too sensitive are simply not documented.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: Therefore, our starting point should be prioritising transparency that leads to good governance and an informed citizenry instead of transparency for its own sake.

sections.label: SG60 Heart&Soul Experience
sections.summary: The SG60 Heart&Soul Experience drew two million visitors and let Singaporeans express hopes and dreams for Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: The SG60 Heart&Soul Experience, which was visited by two million visitors in the second half of last year, allowed Singaporeans to express their hopes and dreams for Singapore.

sections.label: NAIC role and NAIS 2.0
sections.summary: A Member asked about NAIC's authority and integration with MTI and MDDI, and about progress on NAIS 2.0.

sentences.speaker: The Chairman
sentences.text: I will prioritise Members who have filed cuts according to the amount of time they have filed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
sentences.text: I believe the Minister did not get an opportunity to address my cut on the role of NAIC.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
sentences.text: Will it have execution authority or oversee cross-Ministry implementation or remain advisory?

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
sentences.text: And how will the NAIC integrate economic strategy under MTI with digital governance under MDDI to ensure a coordinated delivery?

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
sentences.text: Also, on NAIS 2.0, what progress has been made and what did we learn from implementing NAIS 2.0 that will shape our current plans?

sections.label: Trusted AI certification and NAIS 2.0
sections.summary: A Member asked about a trusted AI certification regime and what was learned from NAIS 2.0, launched December 2023.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
sentences.text: Will we consider establishing a formal trusted AI certification regime for high-risk AI systems deployed in finance, healthcare and aviation?

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Perhaps to address Mr Sharael Taha's question on what we have learned from the implementation of NAIS 2.0, the Prime Minister launched NAIS 2.0 in December 2023.

sections.label: Lorong AI growth and Kampong AI
sections.summary: Lorong AI hosted about 150 events with 4,000 people last year, giving confidence to do Kampong AI.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: It turned out to move a lot faster and grow a lot bigger than we expected.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: I think last year, Lorong AI hosted something like 150 events with about 4,000 people.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Because of that, we have the confidence to do Kampong AI.

sections.label: JTC and NAIC purpose
sections.summary: Without JTC's involvement this growth could not have come about, and the NAIC exists to do these things.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: If JTC has not been seized with this idea, then this growth could not have quite come about.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: So, the NAIC is precisely to do these things.

sections.label: Prime Minister chairs National AI Council
sections.summary: The Prime Minister chairing the National AI Council indicates keenness to make AI transformation real for all Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Our Prime Minister has many things on his plate.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: He advises us on a whole range of things, but to chair the National AI Council is a very strong indication that we are keen on making AI transformation real for all Singaporeans and not just something that just continues to exist as a vision.

sections.label: AI safety and online safety institutions
sections.summary: A digital trust centre as designated AI Safety Institute and a Centre of Advanced Technologies for Online Safety have been set up.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: For example, quite apart from introducing model governance frameworks, we have set up a digital trust centre that is our designated AI Safety Institute.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: We also have the Centre of Advanced Technologies for Online Safety.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: These are institutions that have grown within academic organisations, but we will look for opportunities to collaborate with industry, with academia, to see how we can institutionalise this capability and turn it into an advantage for Singapore.

sections.label: Intermediaries and Productivity Solutions Grant
sections.summary: Intermediaries' interest is welcomed, with enterprise solutions largely offered through the Productivity Solutions Grant, about 30% AI-enabled.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: There is very strong interest from these intermediaries to get the word out and we welcome their interest.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: We already have existing programmes that serve as a useful base so, for example, the enterprise solutions will very largely be offered through the Productivity Solutions Grant scheme.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: The Productivity Solutions Grant is well known to many of our enterprises.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: I mentioned in my earlier speech that about 30% of the solutions are now AI-enabled.

sections.label: Starting with accountancy and legal
sections.summary: For individuals, work will start with the accountancy and legal professions, then extend to fields like HR.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: For individuals, I mentioned that we will start, initially, with the accountancy and legal professions and then look to extend towards fields like human resources (HR).

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: HR, for example, easily has 50,000 members, 50,000 practitioners.

sections.label: Elections online advertising legislation
sections.summary: The passage states that where existing legislation, laws and measures are not enough, the Elections (Integrity of Online Advertising), or ELIONA, legislation was introduced.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: But there will be instances where existing legislation, existing laws, existing measures are not enough.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: So, for example, we introduced the Elections (Integrity of Online Advertising), or ELIONA, legislation.

sections.label: AI translation for public services
sections.summary: The National Translation Committee is working with GovTech and A*STAR on LLMs to fine-tune a local-context model for translating English public materials into Malay, Mandarin and Tamil.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
sentences.text: The National Translation Committee has been working with GovTech and Agency for Science, Technology and Research (A*STAR) on a number of LLMs and to fine tune a model for a local context.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
sentences.text: One of the objectives is to, hopefully, have a model which we can use by the later part of this year, to allow greater inclusivity and accessibility for those not speaking English to access our public-facing websites and other materials.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
sentences.text: And to support Public Service agencies translate many of the material, which is in English, into different mother tongue languages – Malay, Mandarin, Tamil – much more easily.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
sentences.text: And how can we do so across the board, at-scale, across the Public Service?

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
sentences.text: So, we are developing an AI tool for that and we hope to share more details in the later part of the year, but this is just one specific example how we are using AI technology.

sections.label: Optimising speed security cost trust
sections.summary: The passage states that one dimension cannot be optimised over another, and that Singapore must optimise across all dimensions: speed, security, cost and trust.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
sentences.text: And so, we cannot afford to optimise one dimension over another.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
sentences.text: It is very educational, and I hope more Singaporeans can understand that we must optimise across all dimensions – speed, security, cost and trust.

sections.label: Thanks to MDDI and Members
sections.summary: The speaker thanks Minister Josephine Teo, Senior Minister of State Tan Kiat How, Minister of State Rahayu, Minister of State Jasmin Lau, the MDDI Permanent Secretary and team, and GPC and Members.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, I would like to take this opportunity to thank Minister Josephine Teo, Senior Minister of State Tan Kiat How, Minister of State Rahayu, Minister of State Jasmin Lau and the Permanent Secretary of MDDI, and the whole MDDI team for the responses and the great work that they do.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
sentences.text: I would also like to thank our GPC and fellow Members for submitting 25 cuts and with more than three hours of debate, leaving no stone unturned; and I am quite sure quite a few of us would like to ask a few more supplementary questions.

sections.label: MDDI tasks and amendment withdrawal
sections.summary: The passage states MDDI must drive innovation, safeguard trust, develop skills, protect the vulnerable and secure national competitiveness, and the speaker seeks leave to withdraw an amendment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
sentences.text: — MDDI must juggle many things at once, drive innovation, safeguard trust, develop the deep and broad-based skill sets, protect the vulnerable and secure national competitiveness.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
sentences.text: That is no small task, and I would like to thank our team in MDDI for doing all of that.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
sentences.text: And with that, Mr Chairman, I seek leave to withdraw my amendment.
